claims.text: Chiari malformation (CM): the cerebellum pushes down into the spinal canal, which can cause headaches and balance problems.
claims.quote: In CM, the lower part of the brain that controls balance—called the cerebellum—pushes downward into the spinal canal. This can cause headaches and balance problems.

claims.text: Diagnosis: often made after an imaging test such as MRI.
claims.quote: People are often diagnosed with having a CM after an imaging test such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

claims.text: Symptoms can include headache that gets worse with coughing, sneezing, or straining.
claims.quote: Headache that gets worse with coughing, sneezing, or straining

claims.text: Type I is the most common: the lower cerebellum extends at least one-fifth of an inch into the spinal canal.
claims.quote: This is the most common type. It’s typically diagnosed when the lower part of the cerebellum pushes downward into the space that holds the spinal cord by at least one-fifth of an inch.
claims.locator: Types of CM, CM Type I

claims.text: Type I is often found in teens and adults imaged for headaches, dizziness, or balance problems.
claims.quote: Doctors usually find out that teenagers and adults have a CM Type I while doing tests to find the cause of neurological symptoms such as headaches, dizziness, or balance problems.
claims.locator: Types of CM, CM Type I

claims.text: Type II (Arnold-Chiari) occurs with a myelomeningocele, a type of spina bifida.
claims.quote: Infants with a CM Type II also have a myelomeningocele—a type of spina bifida
claims.locator: Types of CM, CM Type II

claims.text: Type II is also called Arnold-Chiari malformation.
claims.quote: CM Type II is also called Arnold-Chiari malformation.
claims.locator: Types of CM, CM Type II

claims.text: Associated conditions: hydrocephalus, spina bifida, syringomyelia, tethered cord.
claims.quote: CM is associated with other neurological conditions, including: Hydrocephalus (buildup of spinal fluid in the brain) Spina bifida (bones in the back don’t completely close around the spinal cord before birth) Syringomyelia (a spinal fluid-filled sac in the spinal cord) Tethered spinal cord syndrome

claims.text: Surgery removes a small piece of bone from the back of the skull (sometimes the top of the spine) to give the brain more room.
claims.quote: During surgery, surgeons remove a small piece of bone from the back of the skull (and sometimes the top of the spine) to give the brain more room
